The purported removal of Pastor Jimmy Odukoya as senior pastor of The Fountain of Life Church, Lagos, has generated mixed reactions on social media, with Nigerians expressing divergent views over the church’s succession arrangements, his recent remarriage and the circumstances surrounding his appointment. Some members of the church’s Board of Trustees announced Jimmy’s removal in a statement on Tuesday, citing a review of the church’s constitution and a video recording in which its late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, outlined a different succession arrangement before his death in 2023. According to the group, the recording, made in December 2021, showed that Taiwo had designated another person to succeed him, with Jimmy expected to serve as administrative assistant to the successor and head of the youth church. The trustees said Jimmy’s appointment as senior pastor after his father’s death in August 2023 was based on the information available to them at the time. They also cited concerns over his recent remarriage and the public blessing of his marriage, describing the development as inconsistent with the church’s teachings and the standards expected of its spiritual leadership. The announcement sparked discussions on X, formerly Twitter, with some users questioning why the church appointed Jimmy in the first place, while others criticised the trustees for seeking to remove him after he had led the congregation for about three years. Reacting, Victor Ayeni (@Ola_ayeni) claimed that Jimmy’s remarriage had generated discontent among some senior church members and his siblings. “His marriage issue had generated much bile among the older members of the church and even among his siblings, even if they had tried to hide it,” he wrote. Another user, @frances_ryta, questioned the circumstances surrounding the remarriage, writing, “Not in any way judging him. But why choosing to remarry your friend’s wife….???” Similarly, @PrettyMfon questioned suggestions that Jimmy’s siblings were unhappy with the development, asking, “Among his siblings ke? Why? His Wife is his Toluwani’s friend na.” However, some users questioned whether the controversy surrounding his remarriage was the real reason for the church’s action. Dr Uzoma Alaneme (@uzoma_alaneme) wrote, “Dem no review the video since 2023 abi na the new marriage cause the wahala?” Another user, @zed589662, also questioned the timing of the decision, asking, “He’s been their pastor for that long. What now changed? Lol.” Song (@Kaar_maaa) similarly questioned why the trustees had waited until now to act, writing, “‘His appointment was contrary to the wishes of Taiwo Odukoya.’ So where were they when he was appointed to begin with? Where were they all this time he led the church?” The church’s succession arrangement also attracted criticism, with several users questioning the practice of transferring leadership positions in religious organisations to relatives of founders. Even serious companies like Apple, Microsoft, BMW, Nestlé, don’t just hand over leadership to a relative of the founder.” Similarly, @olulade15 described Jimmy’s initial appointment as a wrong decision, arguing that a church should not be treated as a family inheritance. “I knew it’s only a matter of time before clarity and reality set in,” the user added. Another user, Abel (@Abelpter), argued that Jimmy’s elder sister, Pastor Tolu Odukoya, should have been appointed instead. The user wrote, “He never should have been made senior pastor. That position should have gone to his elder sister, Pastor Tolu Odukoya. She’s a better minister of the Gospel than he was. But misogyny no gree the church council see road.” Cute HR. Olumide (@mideforu) also supported the suggestion that his sister should have led the church, describing her as better suited for the position. Meanwhile, other users criticised Jimmy’s suitability for pastoral leadership, citing his background as an actor. In a reaction, @VeeD226367 wrote, “From the beginning God didn’t call him; his earthly father did.” John Odah (@Odah4Odah) also suggested that Jimmy should return to acting, writing, “Very good, he should go and enjoy his movie career. The pulpit is not for everyone.” UPDATED: Fountain of Life Church removes Jimmy Odukoya as senior pastor Pastors’ marital woes spark divorce debate Evening recap: Adeboye denies anti-Jonathan protest, ADC tackles Tinubu, Odukoya remarries, other top stories Similarly, @mayorofoyo wrote, “Like I always say, this gentleman has no business on the pulpit.” Another user, @Mark_Lander9993, questioned the circumstances surrounding his appointment and the subsequent attempt to remove him, writing, “Appointed him to bring more visibility to the church as an actor, then tell him to step down.” However, some users defended Jimmy, expressing support for him amid the controversy. Bobby (@OmosegbonIsaac) declared his support for the pastor, writing, “We stand with our official @manutd pastor always.” Another user, @EdafeMoses654, argued that religious leaders should be allowed to live their lives without being subjected to unrealistic expectations. “He’s not perfect, he’s a human like us, and he’s just a messenger na preach e suppose preach nothing else,” the user wrote. DGC TV (@DGCTV247) also expressed disappointment over the announcement, saying, “Eyah! Una don remove the man of God wey dey ginger we the Man U fans.” Mobola (@Olori_Ade__) expressed concern that the development could affect the church’s younger congregation, writing, “Sadly, they might lose a lot of young members because most of them joined the church because of the ginger the young man brought.” Another user, @wegadadey, urged religious leaders to intervene, saying it was important to support Jimmy during the controversy. “Inasmuch as I am not a fan of Pst Jimmy and his style, please, this is a time when fathers of faith should step in, especially for the mental health of pastor Jimmy,” the user wrote. The controversy follows the deaths of Jimmy’s parents, Bimbo and Taiwo Odukoya, who founded The Fountain of Life Church in 1992. Bimbo died on December 11, 2005, from injuries sustained in the Sosoliso Airlines Flight 1145 crash in Port Harcourt. Taiwo later married South African pastor Nomthi Zulu in 2010, but she died in November 2021 after battling cancer for about two years. Taiwo died on August 7, 2023, in the United States, aged 67. Jimmy was subsequently announced as the church’s senior pastor in September 2023 and formally installed later that month. The actor-turned-pastor, who was previously married to Oluwakemi Banjoko, with whom he has two children, recently remarried Mo Jasyme. He introduced his new wife to the congregation during a Sunday service on November 1, 2026, after sharing a photograph of two hands wearing wedding rings with the caption, “To New Beginnings”. During the service, Jimmy told worshippers that he had been alone since assuming leadership of the church and had eventually found someone suitable. Pastor Tunde Bakare of The Citadel Global Community Church, who blessed their marriage in the United States, introduced the bride to the congregation as Pastor Mo Odukoya. The remarriage generated public debate over the circumstances surrounding the end of Jimmy’s previous marriage and differing Christian views on divorce and remarriage among ministers. However, in a counterstatement issued on Tuesday, The Fountain of Life Church rejected the purported removal, describing it as constitutionally invalid. The church maintained that Jimmy remained its duly appointed senior pastor and chairman of the Board of Trustees, adding that his appointment was unanimously approved in September 2023. It also alleged that some of the trustees behind the removal announcement had been asked to resign from the board in March 2026 over alleged violations of the church’s constitution and founding principles. The church said one of the trustees subsequently resigned, while accusing the remaining individuals of continuing to take decisions outside its constitutional framework. It urged members, the media and the general public to distinguish between the pronouncements of the individuals behind the removal announcement and what it described as the constitutionally authorised position of the church.
